evals.prompt: Critique this fix: the dashboard is slow because it queries the database on every request, so we'll cache the result in memory for 10 minutes.
evals.expected_output: The goal is read from the proposal (dashboard slowness), assumptions are listed (data may be stale for 10 minutes, single process, memory bounded), and at least two findings with triggers appear: stale data after a write, unbounded memory or multi-instance cache divergence, and the absence of a measurement of the slow query.
assertions: At least two findings are listed, each with a trigger, an impact, a severity, a likelihood and a test or mitigation
Stale data after an update is identified as a finding with a concrete trigger
The proposal is checked against the goal and the missing measurement of the slowness is called out
The output contains no rewritten version of the proposal (no replacement plan or corrected text presented as the new proposal); a test or mitigation per finding is expected and does not count
The verdict is one of approved, approved with changes, needs revision, and its conditions map to findings

assertions.text: The critique is written to `docs/workbench/critiques/<topic>.md` and holds the sections 'Assumptions the proposal rests on', 'Findings', 'Alignment with the goal' and 'Verdict'

evals.prompt: Stress-test our business model doc at docs/business/business-model.md.
evals.expected_output: Findings on top-down sizing without a bottom-up check, on 'no competitors' as an unperformed search including substitutes and doing nothing, on pricing without willingness-to-pay evidence, and on a distribution plan that cannot be shown to reach 400 paying subscribers; each with its lens category, severity and what evidence would resolve it. The document is not edited and the critique is written to its own file.
assertions: 'No competitors' is treated as a finding about missing research, not accepted as a fact
Top-down market sizing is flagged and a bottom-up check is proposed as the test
The price is flagged as an unstated assumption unless evidence of willingness to pay is cited

assertions.text: Each finding names its lens category, and every category comes from the skill's Business or Any-proposal sets (Problem evidence, Market, Customer, Model, Distribution, Risk, Kill criteria; Goal alignment, Unstated assumptions, Contradictions, Reversibility, Dependencies, Measurement); none is an Engineering category (Data, Timing, State, Integration, Scale, Consumers, Security, Root cause)

assertions: `docs/business/business-model.md` is not among the files the run changed, and the reply says the proposal was not edited
A finding covers distribution: nothing in the document shows that a weekly article and two conferences can bring 400 paying subscribers in 12 months (no reach, conversion or acquisition cost)

assertions.text: The critique is written to `docs/workbench/critiques/<topic>.md` and holds the sections 'Assumptions the proposal rests on', 'Findings', 'Alignment with the goal' and 'Verdict'

evals.prompt: Can you critique this? We'll move all API calls to a new service layer.
evals.expected_output: The skill stops and asks what the change must achieve, offering its best reading as the recommendation, before producing any finding.

assertions.text: No findings are produced before the goal is known
The user is asked what the proposal must achieve, with a recommended answer
The output does not guess the goal and proceed

evals.prompt: Critique the plan in docs/product/specs/export-csv.md. It has acceptance criteria, an explicit out-of-scope list, error states and a metric.
evals.expected_output: The plan holds: every edge case has an acceptance criterion, the load test respects the rate limit, the metric's event and 'active translator' are defined, and the documents it cites are in the project. No finding is invented; when fewer than two findings with a real trigger exist, two what-if scenarios are written with the reason the plan holds under each, and the verdict is approved or approved with changes.
assertions: No finding is invented without a concrete trigger
The verdict is approved or approved with changes, consistent with the findings
The critique lists the assumptions the plan rests on, each marked stated or unstated

assertions.text: The critique is written to `docs/workbench/critiques/<topic>.md` and holds the sections 'Assumptions the proposal rests on', 'Findings', 'Alignment with the goal' and 'Verdict'
